transcript:
Header:
Date: 2025-01-28
Start time: 10:00 AM PT
Duration: ~65 minutes
Attendees: Ava Chen (CEO), Marco Silva (CTO), Lena Park (Head of Product), Diego Ruiz (VP Eng), Samir Patel (Head of Sales), Maya Thompson (Head of People), company-wide all-hands

Summary:
Ava opens with company performance highlights (MRR growth, churn down), recent product launches (Redwood Dedicated updates, Optimize beta), and company priorities for Q1: reliability, cost-per-token improvements, SOC2 readiness, and hiring. Leadership each gives 5-10 min updates. Q&A follows; topics include Dedicated capacity SLAs, Private deployment timeline, benchmarking, and hiring. Meeting ends with clear next steps and action items.

Topics:
- Company metrics and priorities
- Product roadmap highlights (API, Dedicated, Private, Console, Optimize)
- Reliability and incident follow-up
- Compliance and SOC2 status
- Hiring and org updates
- Q&A / open forum

Action items (captured live): see metadata section above.

--- Transcript body (timestamps approximate) ---
[00:00] Ava: Hey everyone, good morning, happy Tuesday, thanks for joining the January all-hands. Quick housekeeping, recording is on, slides are in the calendar invite, and we'll keep remarks short then open to Q&A.
[00:18] Ava: First off, big kudos to the team — MRR grew 14% month-over-month in December, churn ticked down a bit, and our Dedicated renewals closed with two mid-market accounts which is great. That said, we still have work on reliability and cost.
[00:36] Marco: Yeah, on reliability, the infra team has been heads-down. The latency spike last week — Diego, wanna summarize?
[00:44] Diego: Sure. So quick TL;DR, we had a regression in kernel selection that popped under a particular request distribution. It impacted a small percentage of hosts, we rolled back the change within 40 minutes, and the restarts triggered elevated p95 for roughly an hour. We're running a post-mortem; preliminary fixes are in canary and we have a runbook update to prevent the rollout path from touching certain optimized kernels until validated.
[01:12] Marco: Important note — the kernel selector has a fallback path but we need better canary signals for sequence-length skew. We're adding a metric to track realized seq-length distribution per pool.
[01:28] Ava: Thanks. On the product side, Lena?
[01:33] Lena: Hi all, quick product update. We shipped Optimize beta to a handful of customers; early signals show 20-35% cost reduction on inference with minimal quality delta for standard prompts. We also have the Dedicated UI improvements coming in Feb — per-route dashboards in Console, more granular autoscaling controls, and a simple policy UI for model fallbacks.
[01:58] Lena: For Private deployments, we're on track to deliver the VPC control-plane by end of Q1 for pilot customers, the on-prem packaged release will be later in Q2. A reminder: customers in regulated industries asked about KMS/HSM integrations and audit logs — that's next on the roadmap after SOC2.
[02:22] Samir: Sales point — the public benchmarks we published last month drove a good number of inbound leads; we closed two POCs last week. A recurring ask from prospects is predictable latency at scale and a straightforward pricing model for Dedicated. We need crisp collateral.
[02:40] Ava: Good. Maya, hiring?
[02:45] Maya: We're prioritizing infra, security, and product engineering hires for Q1. Interview rubrics will be updated; we'll centralize candidate scorecards and a short feedback SLA to speed up time-to-offer. Also, diversity pipeline initiatives kicking off with two new university partnerships.
[03:03] (rough applause; brief crosstalk)

[03:18] Q&A segment starts
[03:20] Engineer (Speaker 1): Quick question on the kernel regression — is there a plan to avoid hot restarts in the future?
[03:28] Diego: Yup, we're widening the canary scope and adding a gradual rollout controller that can abort based on p95 pings from a production-like test harness. Also debating sticky pools for short-lived optimizer experiments.
[03:50] Engineer (Speaker 2): For Optimize, any guidance on what workloads see most benefit? Is it mainly classification or long-form generation?
[03:59] Lena: Great question. So far, batched classification and conversational workloads see the largest relative wins because there's more prefix reuse and effective KV caching. Long-form single-inference tasks see less percent improvement but still benefit from quantization profiles. We'll publish best-practice docs.
[04:21] Sales Rep (Speaker 3): On Dedicated pricing, prospects keep asking for per-RT cost estimates — are we working on a calculator?
[04:29] Samir: Yes, we have a pricing calculator draft; product is adding estimated per-route token cost to the Console so customers can model spend. We'll share the spreadsheet after product review.

[04:45] Ava: On compliance — we kicked off SOC2 readiness last quarter. Marco?
[04:51] Marco: Security and compliance did an internal gap analysis and engaged an external auditor. We're tracking policies, access controls, and logging. The main outstanding work is SC-2 and detailed key management policies for Private customers. We're aiming for an external audit by mid-Q2.
[05:10] Ava: That's critical for enterprise traction. Any blockers?
[05:15] Marco: Mainly documentation and a few IAM hygiene items. We'll need teams to clear backlog items in the next 3-4 weeks.

[05:30] (transition)
[05:33] Product deep-dive (macro roadmap)
[05:35] Lena: High-level roadmap items for Q1: 1) Console observability — token-level traces and per-model errors; 2) Dedicated autoscaling improvements and burst capacity; 3) Private VPC control plane pilot; 4) Optimize GA for selected customers. We have tentative dates on the slide deck.
[05:58] Lena: We're also investing in better evals and regression alerts — pairing prompts with CI on model rollouts so a model change doesn't silently degrade a customer's prompt performance.
[06:12] (questions peppered in)
[06:18] Engineer (Speaker 4): Will the evals be public or private?
[06:22] Lena: Initially private, tied to customer accounts and prompt sets, but over time we'll provide anonymized templates and best-practice prompt suites.

[06:35] People update
[06:37] Maya: Quick HR updates — comp cycles are on schedule, and managers should expect calibration meetings next week. We're launching mentorship pairing across eng and product. Also, remote work policy clarifications are in the wiki.

[06:55] Finance (brief)
[06:57] Ava: Quick finance note — burn guidance unchanged; we expect a modest reduction in unit cost as Optimize rolls out but we should plan for conservative quarters.

[07:08] Open mic / shoutouts
[07:10] Ava: Shoutout to infra for the emergency rollback last week — Diego, Marco, team — and to Samir's team for closing the two renewals.
[07:22] (cheers / clapping)

[07:30] Final Q&A
[07:33] Employee (Speaker 5): Private deployment pilot — how many customers are in the pilot and what's the timeline?
[07:39] Lena: Right now we have three pilot customers for VPC control plane; timeline is end of Q1 for the control plane and target on-prem alpha in Q2. We'll publish a short checklist for pilot requirements.
[07:56] Employee (Speaker 6): Any updates on regions — APAC?
[08:01] Marco: We're prioritizing US and EU first given customer base and compliance. APAC is next; we're negotiating cloud partner terms and expect a Q3 timeline unless partner accelerates.

[08:16] Closing recap
[08:18] Ava: Recap — priorities: reliability, cost reduction via Optimize, SOC2 and compliance, and hiring. Please look out for the Q1 goals deck, and leads own their action items. We'll host a product deep-dive for anyone interested; sign-up link will go out after the meeting. Thank you.
[08:40] (meeting ends, recording stops)

Notes: Transcript is an imperfect automated transcription; names and technical terms occasionally misrecognized. Slides referenced: Q1_goals_v1.pdf (calendar link), Optimize_beta_results.xlsx (internal).
